native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (operationalized as ever_jailed, jailed during 1985-1994) were found to have significantly lower composite wealth than those without in ALL three measured years: 1985 (Holm-adj p=1.60e-10), 1990 (Holm-adj p=2.34e-34), and 1996 (Holm-adj p=1.86e-25); the association persists after controlling race and sex and is correlational, not causal.
native_result.WorkflowB: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U per year (1985/1990/1996) on composite_wealth comparing ever_jailed=1 vs 0; Holm-Bonferroni correction across the 3 years; effect size via Hodges-Lehmann median difference with rank-based 95% CI plus bootstrap; robustness via permutation mean-difference test and median quantile regression adjusting for race and sex (sensitivity only). Data have no missing values; zeros treated as genuine values (ties); heavy skew handled by rank-based methods.

sub_hypo.text: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, with wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Individuals jailed between 1985 and 1994 (ever_jailed = 1) have significantly lower composite wealth in each of 1985, 1990, and 1996 than individuals not jailed during that period (ever_jailed = 0).

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals jailed during 1985–1994 had significantly lower composite wealth than individuals not jailed during that period in all three measured years (1985, 1990, and 1996). The association persists after controlling for race and sex and is correlational, not causal.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, comparing incarceration status during 1985–1994 and composite wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Composite wealth is significantly lower for ever_jailed=1 than for ever_jailed=0 in 1985 (Holm-adjusted p=1.60e-10), 1990 (p=2.34e-34), and 1996 (p=1.86e-25), using two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction across the three years. The association persists in sensitivity analyses using median quantile regression adjusting for race and sex; it is correlational, not causal.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Individuals with a criminal record (operationalized as ever_jailed, jailed during 1985-1994) were found to have significantly lower composite wealth than those without in ALL three measured years: 1985 (Holm-adj p=1.60e-10), 1990 (Holm-adj p=2.34e-34), and 1996 (Holm-adj p=1.86e-25); the association persists after controlling race and sex and is correlational, not causal.
